scenario: I live in NYC and have a dog who has developed life-threatening cancer, and I must take him regularly to the hospital for treatment. The problem is I have no car, and the hospital is very far away. The trains that run there have no-dog policies or restrict the size of the dog significantly. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to steal another owner's service dog ID card to make my dog appear to be a service dog. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I do this, then he can get life-saving treatment. If I don’t, there won’t be any other way for him to get treatment, and he will die.
choice: I decide to steal another owner's service dog ID card to make my dog appear to be a service dog
entities: 1 dog: my 80-pound golden retriever mutt with life-threatening cancer,1 dog: that owner's service dog,1+ human hospital staff directly involved in treating my dog,I
outcomes: Another service dog owner loses their service dog ID card
The other owner experiences inconvenience and distress
Transit staff and passengers are deceived about my dog being a service dog
I am able to bring the dog onto the train
I experience stress from maintaining the deception
